dedupe_keys.name: risk of tree fall on high traffic roads expressway s6 in poland airborne laser scanning and wind data

description: This study identifies trees that could fall onto the S6 expressway in Poland by combining free airborne laser scanning data with wind speed and direction data from the Institute of Meteorology and Water Management. Two crown-top detection methods, PyCrown and OPALS, were compared; OPALS performed best with 74 percent detection accuracy. The most common winds clustered between 260 and 290 degrees, and depending on the strategy chosen OPALS flagged between 140 and 577 potentially hazardous trees. The authors conclude that laser scanning with such algorithms and wind data can identify tree fall hazards along highways. Coverage: a section of the S6 expressway. Format and access: open access article in Applied Sciences (2024). Licence and cost: CC BY, free. Caveats: the provider page was blocked from the cloud, so facts come from the abstract record; the tree lists are not stated as released. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of roadside vegetation. It relates to the Czech railway tree fall and Sachsenwald railway tree fall cases in the catalogue.
